comparison: Perfect agreement on APP-LRP4 interaction (C4, C31, C65, C66, C105). Both evaluations find the biochemical evidence strong and convincing, with reviewers explicitly affirming the demonstration is 'strong and convincing.'

Agreement on APP-agrin binding data (C5, C32, C82, C90, C91, C107). Both accept the binding observations as valid, though peer reviewers raise concerns about functional interpretation (whether APP aggregates agrin) rather than the binding data itself.

Agreement on cooperative binding data (C6, C84, C85, C86, C108). Both evaluations accept the biphasic modulation data without questioning the biochemical observations, though peer reviewers focus concerns on functional interpretation.

Disagreement on MuSK phosphorylation claims (C33, C69-C74, C106). OpenEval finds the dose-response data convincing with appropriate controls. Peer reviewers challenge the interpretation that APP-LRP4 can activate MuSK independently of agrin, noting C2C12 cells express muscle agrin and requesting experiments in agrin-/- cells.

Partial disagreement on AChR clustering (C7, C67, C68). OpenEval accepts the clustering data as supporting APP's functional role. Peer reviewers question whether the mechanism is truly demonstrated due to endogenous muscle agrin in C2C12 cells, requesting additional experiments.

Partial overlap on genetic epistasis (C75-C77). OpenEval finds the knockout data clearly demonstrate APP's dependence on LRP4/MuSK. Peer reviewers question the in vitro clustering interpretation due to confounding agrin expression, suggesting additional experiments.
Agreement on complex formation (C78-C81). Both evaluations accept the co-IP data demonstrating LRP4-APP-MuSK complex formation in vivo without questioning the biochemical evidence.
Agreement on LRP4-APLP2 genetic interaction (C64, C112). Both evaluations accept the morphological and survival data demonstrating genetic interaction without raising concerns.

Disagreement on prepatterning independence (C92, C93). OpenEval finds the immunofluorescence data clearly establish independence. Peer reviewers request additional evaluation of APP/APLP2 requirement for prepatterning, suggesting existing data is insufficient.

Disagreement on LRP4 localization data (C94-C102). OpenEval finds the developmental changes well-documented. Peer reviewers explicitly state it is 'unclear if APP and LRP4 are expressed in a spatially and temporally correlated manner' and request additional expression profiling.
Agreement on compensatory LRP4 upregulation (C103, C104, C119). Both evaluations accept the Western blot and qPCR data showing increased LRP4 expression in mutants without challenge.

Disagreement on hetero-oligomeric complex model (C34, C35, C109, C114). OpenEval finds the cooperative binding and functional data collectively support the model. Peer reviewers challenge the mechanistic interpretation, stating conclusions about APP-LRP4 activating MuSK are 'not supported by the data shown' due to confounding factors.

Disagreement on trans-synaptic adhesion model (C110, C111, C113). OpenEval accepts the established literature and localization data. Peer reviewers note the model is 'tempting to speculate' but recommend additional experiments with APP-/- motoneuron cultures to test the hypothesis.

Disagreement on APP-LRP4 genetic interaction severity (C9-C11, C62, C63). OpenEval finds the quantitative data and perinatal lethality clearly demonstrate synergistic interaction. Peer reviewers note the impairment appears 'subtle' in fluorescent images and request quantitative analysis to show significance.

Agreement on normal maturation events (C52-C57). Both evaluations accept that synapse elimination and subunit switch occur normally in Lrp4ECD/ECD mice. Peer reviewers use this to challenge broader conclusions about maturation.

Strong disagreement on membrane anchoring requirement for maturation (C115-C118). OpenEval finds the phenotypic comparison supports the model. Peer reviewers explicitly state this conclusion 'seems to be a misinterpretation' because many maturation events are 'apparently normal' in ECD/ECD mice.

Partial overlap on Lrp4ECD/ECD phenotype (C8, C39, C40, C49). OpenEval finds multiple lines of evidence support impaired growth with normal initial formation. Peer reviewers question the significance of the double mutant phenotype and request quantitative analysis.

Disagreement on LBD domain requirement (C65). OpenEval accepts the domain mapping as part of the interaction evidence. Peer reviewers state 'There was no data to show that this domain was required for fl LRP4 interaction with APP' and request functional experiments testing if APP-induced clustering requires the LBD.

Minimal overlap on ECD phenotype distinction (C38). OpenEval finds the immunofluorescence clearly distinguishes null from ECD phenotypes. This claim appears in peer R6 which questions the double mutant significance.
Minimal overlap on maturation claims (C58). OpenEval includes this in broader support for the membrane anchoring model. Peer reviewers explicitly reject the maturation interpretation.

OpenEval finds morphological analysis (C45-C48) demonstrates normal NMJ formation in Lrp4ΔICD/ΔICD mice, with consistency to cattle mutation strengthening conclusions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific claims about the ICD deletion phenotype.
OpenEval accepts background claims about APP, ApoE, and Alzheimer's disease (C1, C12-C17, C21-C24) as well-established literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts background claims about APP family function at synapses (C2, C3, C18-C20) based on prior literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts background claims about CNS expression and AD relevance (C25-C30) based on literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts established knowledge about NMJ development (C41, C60, C61) based on citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts established knowledge about agrin isoforms (C88, C89, C120) based on literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval accepts cattle mutation validation (C47, C48) based on citation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds Wnt modulator role (C123-C125) speculative without experimental data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval finds muscle agrin regulatory mechanism (C121, C122) plausible but requiring validation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
